label: claude-haiku-4.5
judgeModel: claude-opus-5 (via Claude Code CLI, first-party, owner subscription)
method: v2: judged against the FULL production source text, not the 5,000-char clipped bundle excerpt. Judge is Opus 5 via the Claude Code CLI, billed to the owner subscription, not OpenRouter.

audio.reasoning: All ten claims are grounded in the source text (11.1.4 ch, Dolby Atmos, wireless rear speakers, subwoofer, 11 front-facing speakers, 4 up-firing channels, HDMI ARC/eARC, Alexa/Google Assistant via Chromecast, Q-Symphony), with no cross-product contamination and no retailer star-ratings or nav boilerplate extracted. Minor gap: it captured only specs and skipped the well-documented firmware audio-dropout defect reported across sources 6-9, which is a checkable claim about this product.

tv_display.reasoning: All 12 claims trace to the source text, with correct model-line separation (the 4K 120Hz caveat for the 2.47 m variant is kept intact) and no contamination from the QN800D/S90D/QN85D or Frame bezel boilerplate; retailer star-ratings and template placeholders were correctly skipped. Minor weakness: Dolby Atmos + Object Tracking Sound+ comes from the 43-inch Amazon listing and Bixby/Alexa support comes from generic Samsung TV support pages, not QN90D-specific text, so both are slight generalizations.

computing.reasoning: Several claims are misattributed across generations: claim 1 assigns "15th-gen Core Ultra" to Gen 13 when Source 4 states it about Gen 12 updates, and claims 2-6 come from a Gen 12 listing (Source 5) but are presented as generic X1 Carbon specs. Claims 7-8 mix a 400-nit figure and OLED 2K option from a single Gen 12 listing, and claim 12 is grounded but the extraction never disambiguates which generation each spec belongs to.

wearable_health.reasoning: All eight claims trace to the source text, and the extraction correctly avoided the Google Fitbit Air decoy sources (4 and 5), which is the main contamination trap here. Minor weakness: 'tracks sleep' and 'tracks steps' are inferred from a user complaint thread rather than a spec statement, and it skipped the also-present Google apps integration claim.

kitchen.reasoning: All 11 claims are grounded in the source text and correctly tagged by model number where the sources cover distinct variants (01264 aluminum, 01362 stainless, 02141 electric), and retailer star-ratings were correctly filtered out. Small deductions: the two-year warranty claim comes from SOURCE 11, where it belongs to the Fisher & Paykel wine cabinet, not the Presto cooker (cross-product contamination), and claims 1/10 are stated flatly without the model qualifier the sources attach to them.

cleaning.reasoning: All 12 claims are grounded in the source text with correct model attribution (Jet 60, Jet Bot Combo, AI Jet Ultra, AI Jet Lite kept distinct), and it correctly skipped the junk sources (washer/dryer, SmartThings, dust-bag listings). Minor deduction: it missed the checkable 210AW suction spec from Source 9 and the 280W figure in Source 16, and claims 11/12 are generic line-wide marketing rather than product-specific.

power_charging.reasoning: All nine claims trace directly to the source text (Sources 1, 3, 4, 5), stay on the Anker 737 without pulling in the Prime 250W from Source 9, and skip the Best Buy star-rating and review boilerplate. Minor gap only: it left the priced $109.99/$68.20 and the user-reported 0-100% recharge in about one hour on the table, but nothing extracted is ungrounded.

baby.product: Dr. Brown's Natural Flow Baby Bottles
baby.reasoning: All 12 claims trace to the source text and stay within the Natural Flow / Options+ line, with junk (star counts, prices, Amazon Live boilerplate, the Comotomo comparison) correctly excluded. Minor slip: the Level 2 medium-flow nipple and breast-like latch claim come from a wide-neck nipple listing, and the size list mixes narrow and wide-neck variants without noting the model split.

smart_home.reasoning: All six claims trace to the source text (10" display, 2 microphones, camera from Source 5; video calls from Sources 5/10; Gemini support from Source 6), with no cross-product contamination from the Pixel 10a, Temperature Sensor, or Nest Hub 2nd Gen listings, and no retailer prices or star-ratings pulled in as specs. Minor deduction: claims 5 and 6 are duplicates of the same Gemini fact from the same source.

outdoor.reasoning: The source contains no checkable claims about the CamelBak Chute Mag: Source 1 is Amazon Live blurb plus site-wide footer boilerplate, Source 2 is a different product (Pure Bottle 2.2L), and Source 3 is a third-party replacement lid listing. Returning zero claims is the honest answer here.
